About Overview Energy

Overview Energy is a mission-driven team committed to building a new layer of energy infrastructure: satellites in geosynchronous orbit that redirect solar energy to terrestrial solar projects via passively safe near-infrared light. We're in the earliest phase, where the ground beacon our satellites will point to is aligned, characterized, and field-corrected end-to-end by a small, dedicated team. Headquartered in the Northern Virginia / Washington, DC area and backed by world-class investors, we are advancing the next generation of clean energy technology.

About the Role

We're looking for an Optics Intern to help with the design and building of our ground beacon from the optical bench to a field test site. The beacon is the pointing reference the satellite system will depend on. If it isn't aligned and characterized correctly, nothing downstream works.

You'll work hands-on with the emitter and the observational telescope: aligning the laser, characterizing its output, and co-aligning the beacon with the telescope. Then you'll own a problem we haven't solved yet. Once the system is transported to the test site, alignment may shift. You'll design the procedure that brings it back.

This internship supports our program under a Department of War (DoW) energy investment program. You'll work alongside our optics and hardware engineers, and your alignment data will feed directly into hardware decisions we make.

What You'll Do

- Align the beacon laser within its emitter and verify pointing outside the emitter aperture

- Characterize laser output - power, beam profile, divergence, and pointing stability - and document the results

- Co-align the beacon laser with the observational telescope and verify boresight

- Design a repeatable field alignment procedure that corrects misalignment introduced during transport and installation at the DoW site

- Write that procedure so a non-optics operator can execute it, then validate it hands-on before delivery

- Maintain clean alignment and characterization records, and feed findings back to the engineering team

What We're Looking For From You

- Currently enrolled in a bachelor's or master's program in optics, optical engineering, physics, or a closely related field

- Coursework or lab experience with optical alignment: mounts, mirrors, lenses, and beam paths

- Willingness to complete laser safety training and follow protocol without exception

- Careful documentation habits - alignment work is only useful if it's repeatable by someone else

- Able to commit approximately 10 hours per week from September 2026 through March 2027, on-site in Northern Virginia

We Have a Strong Preference For

- Hands-on use of beam profilers, power meters, autocollimators, or shear plates

- Telescope operation or astronomical instrumentation experience

- Zemax OpticStudio, Quadoa, Code V, or comparable optical design and analysis software

- Experience writing test or alignment procedures that other people have actually followed

- Demonstrated interest in defense, space, or energy applications

Internship Details

This is a paid, part-time internship running September 2026 through March 2027 at approximately 10 hours per week, based on-site at our Northern Virginia headquarters. Hourly rate: $30-$40.

You'll be mentored directly by the engineers running the program, and your work is a funded DoW deliverable, not a side project. Interns are not eligible for the full-time benefits package.

ITAR Requirements

This position is subject to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR). Candidates must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident, protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State.

Equal Opportunity Employer

Overview Energy is an Equal Opportunity Employer. If you require a reasonable accommodation during the application process, please contact us at talent@overviewenergy.com.

About Parspec

Founded in 2021, Parspec is revolutionizing the materials supply chain for the $13 trillion USD construction industry by digitizing and organizing the industry's product data. Our proprietary AI technology maintains a current and comprehensive catalogue of millions of products, enabling our customers to instantly identify the products that best meet their needs. Trusted by top designers, builders, distributors, manufacturers, and sales agents, and backed by leading venture investors, Parspec is paving the way for a more innovative, connected, and sustainable future in construction.

Join us in building transformative technology that reshapes one of the world's oldest and largest industries.

The Opportunity

What does it take to turn an AI agent into a product customers trust and pay for? That question sits at the heart of this internship.

We are looking for an intern to work alongside Parspec's product leadership on our AI quoting agent, the product at the center of how distributors and rep agencies build quotes. You will own a piece of it end to end, from customer discovery through an engineering-ready product spec, and help shape the business model behind it. Quoting is the beating heart of our customers' business. It is also messy, manual, and full of judgment calls, which is exactly what makes it both a hard and a valuable problem for an AI agent to take on.

This is not a shadowing role. You will talk to real customers, write requirements that engineers build against, and build prototypes. If you see yourself becoming an AI product leader or founding a company someday, this is a chance to work on the two problems that define AI product management right now: making agents reliable and making them commercially viable.

What You Will Achieve and Key Responsibilities

Define what to build

- Interview distributor and rep agency users to understand how quotes get built today, step by step, including the workarounds and judgment calls that never show up in a process diagram

- Map the quoting workflow end to end and identify where an AI agent delivers the most value, and where human judgment needs to stay in the loop

- Turn what you learn into a clear, prioritized view of what the agent should do next, backed by customer evidence rather than intuition

Prototype and validate

- Build working prototypes to test agent workflows with real users before engineering commits to a full build

- Translate customer needs into product requirements and an engineering-ready spec for your piece of the agent

- Define the success metrics that tell us the agent is actually working: accuracy, time saved, trust, and adoption

- Set the release criteria the agent must meet before it reaches customers, including how we evaluate reliability on real-world quoting scenarios

Shape AI pricing

- Analyze the value the agent creates for customers, how usage actually behaves, and what it costs us to serve

- Study how other AI products charge for agentic work, from seats to usage to outcomes, and what those models would mean for our customers and our margins

- Recommend how Parspec should charge for AI-powered work, with the analysis to back it up, and present it to leadership

Why This Matters

Every software company is racing to put AI agents in front of customers. Very few have figured out the two things that actually matter: making the agent reliable enough that customers trust it with real work, and pricing it so the business works. Parspec is live in the market with AI doing real quoting work for real customers, which means these are not thought experiments here. The quality bar you set shapes what customers experience, and the pricing model you recommend shapes how the company grows. Few internships put you that close to the decisions that matter.

Who You Are

You are curious about how products get built and sold. You like talking to users as much as you like working through data, and you can hold both the customer's reality and the business model in your head at the same time. You write clearly, you ask sharp questions, and you are comfortable forming a view on a problem nobody has fully solved yet. You are not afraid to roll up your sleeves and go deep into a messy workflow to map complex processes and identify how AI can enhance them. You do not need to be an AI engineer, but you need to be genuinely curious about how AI agents work, what makes them fail, and what makes people trust them.

Mandatory Qualifications

- Currently pursuing or recently completed a degree (undergraduate or graduate) in Business, Economics, Engineering, Computer Science, Data Analytics, or a related field

- Strong analytical skills, including comfort working through usage data, unit economics, and pricing trade-offs

- Structured problem-solving ability: you can break an ambiguous question down into an answerable workplan

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to run a customer interview and write a spec an engineer can build from

- A real ownership mentality: you have taken something from question to shipped result without being managed through it

- Genuine interest in AI products: you have used them seriously, formed opinions on what works and what does not, and can articulate why

Preferred Experience

- Prior professional experience in product management, consulting, software engineering, or a startup operating role

- Hands-on experience building with or evaluating LLMs and AI agents, even on personal projects

- Exposure to B2B SaaS business models, pricing and packaging work, or product discovery methods

- Interest in construction, building materials, industrial distribution, or vertical SaaS businesses

- Experience in fast-paced or early-stage startup environments

What We Offer

- Direct, sustained working exposure to Parspec's product leadership

- Ownership of a live piece of an AI product that real customers use, with a spec and a pricing recommendation the company acts on

- Hands-on experience with the two defining challenges of AI product management: making agents reliable and making them commercially viable

- A strong foundation and a credible story for future roles in AI product management, product leadership, or founding

- Flexible hybrid work environment

Join Us and Lead the Transformation!

At Parspec, we recognize that traditional job descriptions don't always capture the full range of your unique abilities, and that's perfectly okay. You may not meet every requirement, but if you bring a mix of experiences, fresh perspectives, and a passion that aligns with our mission, we want to hear from you!

The Parspec team believes that varied backgrounds drive better outcomes and fuel innovation. We are a team of self-starters who lead from every seat. Meta was built to help people connect and share, and over the last decade our tools have played a critical part in changing how people around the world communicate with one another. With over a billion people using the service and more than fifty offices around the globe, a career at Meta offers countless ways to make an impact in a fast growing organization.

Meta is seeking Research Interns to join our AI Search research team. We are committed to advancing the field of artificial intelligence by making fundamental advances in how AI agents learn from their own experience — improving their search and reasoning workflows, retaining useful knowledge, and transferring those gains to unfamiliar tasks. A central research challenge is making repeated self-improvement reliable when feedback is sparse or noisy.

The intern will work in one of three directions, scoped closer to the start date together with the intern manager:

-Learning to improve research workflows — agents learn better search, tool-use and verification strategies from prior attempts by improving their harness: the workflow, memory, tools and feedback loop around the model. Topics include meta-learning across tasks, automated agent design, and learning from natural-language feedback.

-Persistent memory and continual learning — agents retain useful lessons and update knowledge across tasks, whether in context, in compressed memory, or in weights, without forgetting what they already know. Topics include long-context modeling, context compression, continual learning, and test-time training.

-Learning from imperfect feedback — turning noisy judgments and failed attempts into useful learning signals, and improving the strategy an agent uses to learn, including how it selects and evaluates its next improvement. Topics include reward learning, credit assignment, and learning to learn.

Across all three directions, the key test is whether improvements transfer to new tasks. The goal is to develop novel methods and experiments toward a first-author submission at a leading ML/NLP venue. Recent internships on this team have produced work such as REFRAG, a new architecture for retrieval-augmented generation.

Our internships are twelve (12) to twenty-four (24) weeks long and we have various start dates throughout the year.

Develop novel state-of-the-art methods for self-improving, agentic AI systems, leveraging a range of deep learning and reinforcement learning techniques. The Team

The Automated Driving Advanced Development division bridges TRI research and Toyota products. In partnership with Woven by Toyota, the team is researching and developing an end-to-end learned driving stack that maps sensor inputs directly to planned trajectories.

The Internship

We’re seeking a research intern to investigate how driving policies post-trained in fast, low-fidelity simulation can transfer to higher-fidelity simulation and real-world driving. This is an open research problem: differences in sensor inputs, vehicle dynamics, and other agents can limit transfer, and policies may learn simulator-specific behavior or forget previously learned skills.

You’ll lead an independent research project exploring approaches to sim-to-sim and sim-to-real transfer for sensor-based driving models. You’ll work with Toyota driving data, generative base models, and closed-loop simulation infrastructure, with the goal of producing work suitable for a conference or workshop submission.

The Opportunity

As a research intern on AD2, you will own a standalone research project in sim-to-sim and sim-to-real domain mapping, with the opportunity to:

- Drive your own research: Shape the approach, run experiments, and analyze results, with the independence to set your own direction.

- Publish your findings: The project is designed to produce results suitable for a conference or workshop publication.

- Shape a real autonomy model: The tools and insights you create will help the team post-train our autonomy model more effectively, with the potential to influence the autonomy stack eventually deployed in Toyota vehicles.

- Collaborate with experienced researchers: Work closely with a small team of industry-leading researchers with deep experience in robotics and autonomous driving.

- Work at scale: Use the same large-scale Toyota driving data, base models, and simulation infrastructure the team uses every day.

You can learn more about our work on the Automated Driving Advanced Development team page.

- Design and run experiments using large-scale Toyota driving data, the team’s generative base models, and closed-loop simulation infrastructure.

- Perform closed-loop evaluations across simulators of varying fidelity, and develop metrics that measure how well post-trained behaviors carry over between domains.

About the Role: Ginkgo Bioworks is deploying a massive fleet of Reconfigurable Automation Cells (RACs)—modular, mobile robotic units that snap together like LEGOs to form an autonomous lab. We are looking for an Automation Scientist Intern to be the hands-on force behind this fleet. You will learn how to load, operate, take down, and troubleshoot protocol runs on the most advanced lab automation hardware in the world, pushing our "Nebula" frontier lab towards autonomous operation.

- Master the RAC Platform: Learn to operate and maintain a system of Reconfigurable Automation Cells, designed to support a variety of molecular and cell biology scientific workflows. Over time, you will advance to modifying or writing new protocols for our RAC Automation system.

In the process, you will learn how to carefully handle and prepare reagents and consumables for workflows, do basic monitoring and error recovery of runs and safely dispose of used plates from completed workflows.

- No college degree necessary but some skills in coding, biology or computational biology required.

- "Automation-forward" mindset: you love working with lab automation and making robotic systems run smoother.

- Willingness to do whatever it takes to ensure that existing and new scientific workflows run successfully on our RAC automation system.

Bonus (not required):

- Interest in communications, marketing, social media, and/or short form video
